defense_in_depth_findings.title: reviewed_head is byte-anchored, not commit-anchored
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: validate_approval enforces sha256(git_bytes(reviewed_head, release_path)) == approval.release_sha256 but does not pin which commit reviewed_head is. A forged approval plus forged sha-consistent cycle-NN review naming any other committed head whose release bytes are byte-identical (e.g. 53871f4, the review-banking commit) passes the gate; independently demonstrated in a throwaway committed-byte worktree.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: the release bytes are pinned to the exact sha 1b05c093..., every other approval field is forced by required constants, fixed-identity checks, and sha equalities, so any gate-passing approval necessarily binds byte-identical release, authorization b85b255f..., arithmetic abbf1583..., and an ACCEPT review by the pinned reviewer identity and model — zero authority delta. The committed approval names the true release head 35a607896eab09fe985e43a5aab6eca839a866d9, and the future GO token binds the exact committed approval sha 17f9c197..., so a forged variant cannot ride an honestly created token. Recommend a future contract version pin reviewed_head to the banked release commit explicitly.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Approval bytes are pinned only forward by the future GO token, not backward to a git object
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The wrapper reads the approval and review from the repository working tree; the review is sha-pinned by the approval, but the approval file itself is content-validated rather than compared against committed bytes at a pinned head, so its byte identity is enforced only at token-validation time via token.approval_sha256.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: mutation closure was demonstrated against the committed gate — 30 single-field approval mutations (missing, extra, reordered, duplicate-key, every required constant, identities, all four sha bindings, code head, reviewed head, review path traversal and name, reviewer and approver identity and model) plus 9 forged-chain and in-place tamper attacks and 5 historical-approval substitutions all fail closed with the correct gate labels, so every accepting approval is value-identical to the committed one; the human token ceremony binding the exact sha 17f9c197... is the final checkpoint, and creating that token is explicitly outside this review's authority. Recommend the wrapper additionally verify approval bytes via git at a banked approval head in a future version.

defense_in_depth_findings.title: Ledger adapter remains outside the sha-pinned bindings census at approval time
defense_in_depth_findings.detail: The approval constant ledger=175 is enforced at execution preflight through f017_representative_expert_ledger_adapter_v1 (sha256 3655b90cff0a... at the execution code head), which is still not one of the twelve release bindings; carried forward from release-review DID-1 and re-verified unchanged at the approval target head.
defense_in_depth_findings.disposition: NON_BLOCKING: the adapter and its sole pinned data source (f017-representative-m1f0-real-execution-result-v1.json, sha256 dc53b458fe9c... at the code head) are byte-identical between the code head and the approval target, the adapter is read-only and fail-closed with no checkpoint, shard, or compute capability, and current_ledger() on committed worktree bytes independently returned 175 during this review. Recommend adding the adapter to the bindings census in any future release version.

statement: Independent adversarial approval review of exact committed bytes at 24d0552ffec6679b67c2e7822197a1a4bdafbf62 on feat/017-real-checkpoint-runner. The approval artifact at docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f017-representative-s2-single-use-release-v1-independent-approval-v1.json recomputes from git-show bytes to sha256 17f9c1977327932a73550120704b42e01cb0b83b27fa8cd6647f259982be7949, carries exactly the 28 fields of the sha-pinned approval contract (c391d84b...) in exact contract order with zero missing, extra, or reordered fields, and satisfies every required constant including verdict ACCEPT, approver identity CLAUDE_FABLE_5_INDEPENDENT_APPROVER, approver model claude-fable-5, approval_does_not_execute true, approval_is_not_go_token true, real_event_authorized false, ledger 175, zero checkpoint-read, shard-open, S1-materialization, and FFN-composition budgets, exactly one future S2 construction, and stop boundary AFTER_REPRESENTATIVE_S2_OUTPUT_ONLY. Event, release, and attempt identities match the release exactly (F017-REPRESENTATIVE-S2-PROOF-REFERENCE-DERIVED-1 / -RELEASE-1 / -ATTEMPT-1). Transitive authority recomputed entirely from git-show bytes: release sha 1b05c093... matches the committed release contract byte-for-byte at both the approval's reviewed head 35a607896eab09fe985e43a5aab6eca839a866d9 and the target head; authorization b85b255f..., arithmetic contract abbf1583..., S1 reuse 5c6437f2..., FFN reuse 983b1199..., approval contract c391d84b..., executor c0268b47..., wrapper d99b9100..., terminalizer 70e5e9de..., validator aa718717..., tests d0958f11..., and synthetic rehearsal 71b31bcc... all recompute exactly at execution code head 3c200b62fdd0409d49cd38da4d7cc12405569e60, which is an ancestor of both the reviewed head and the target with only append-only release, review, approval, closeout, and banking commits between (no load-bearing script or contract byte changed), satisfying the release's head semantics. The accepted release review at docs/architecture/reviews/evidence/f017-representative-s2-release-cycle-01-independent-review.json hashes to 5328b829... as bound by the approval, has verdict ACCEPT with empty blocking and non-blocking-required findings, reviewer identity CLAUDE_FABLE_5_INDEPENDENT_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEWER and model claude-fable-5, reviewed head 35a6078..., and matching release, authorization, arithmetic, and code-head bindings, and the reviewed-head release bytes hash exactly to the approval's release sha, closing the git-anchored link. S1 and FFN reuse chains verified transitively without reading machine-local operands: the release-bound reuse authorizations pin S1 operand 8309377ee8e8f34eb91cdb025624144eb5be7821ed9e4a295df29b13aac5a0dd as little-endian f32[6144] (24576 bytes) and FFN operand 4d7aaeb58c4ee33dcaf2329c8cd46234d69ee7f16bb7e6338ac9e0b7a5e6ad1a as little-endian f64[6144] (49152 bytes), and all 14 sub-bindings inside the two reuse authorizations recompute exactly from committed bytes. The frozen proof/reference-derived classification (CANONICAL_F017_PROOF_REFERENCE_DERIVED_S2_SURFACE_INTENTIONALLY_NOT_CLAIMED_EQUIVALENT_TO_PRODUCTION_SERIAL_F32, production equivalence NOT_PROVEN_AND_NOT_CLAIMED) is consistent across release, authorization, and arithmetic contract. Approval/token separation holds: the approval asserts and constant-pins non-execution, the GO token is a disjoint 8-field machine-local artifact requiring real_event_authorized true and binding the exact approval sha, the approval sha appears nowhere in the release, authorization, or arithmetic contract (chain is acyclic: release -> committed review at target head -> independent review -> separate approval -> future machine-local token), and no GO token, receipt, terminal, or S2 execution state exists anywhere in the committed tree. The committed wrapper validate_approval gate was independently exercised in a detached throwaway worktree at the target commit using committed-byte-derived copies only: baseline validate_release and validate_approval pass on committed bytes, and 44 adversarial cases fail closed with the correct gate labels — 30 single-field approval mutations covering missing, extra, reordered, and duplicate fields, every required constant including all budgets and the ledger, identity and statement tampering, release, authorization, arithmetic, and code-head sha substitution, stale reviewed head, review path traversal and name-confinement, and reviewer/approver identity and model substitution; 9 forged-chain attacks including sha-consistent forged cycle-02 reviews with REJECT verdicts, non-empty blocking or non-blocking-required findings, and extra fields, a pre-release stale head (REVIEWED_HEAD_OBJECT), a fully consistent tampered-release forged chain (REVIEWED_RELEASE_BYTES), and an in-place committed-review verdict flip (REVIEW_SHA); and 5 historical approvals from other f017 releases, all rejected at APPROVAL_EXACT_FIELDS_AND_ORDER. One accepted forged variant binding a byte-identical release at an alternate committed head is recorded as DID-A1 with a concrete non-blocking disposition. Accounting is truthful: ledger 175 confirmed by running the committed adapter on committed worktree bytes, all checkpoint, shard, S1, and FFN budgets zero, exactly one future S2 construction, stop boundary enforced by pinned wrapper constants. No real S1 or FFN operand bytes were read and no S2 arithmetic, S1 materialization, FFN composition, checkpoint access, shard open, attempt start, S2 start, or GO token creation was performed during this review; all dynamic testing used a detached committed-byte worktree, restored in place after each tamper case, verified clean, and removed. Three defense-in-depth findings carry concrete non-blocking dispositions; there are no blocking and no non-blocking-required findings. The committed approval safely completes the acyclic release -> review -> approval -> future token chain without itself authorizing execution. Verdict: ACCEPT.
